subject: Exclude the grouping variables in ddply?

messages.author: 15e00b100eff82ec
messages.subject: Exclude the grouping variables in ddply?
parts:
[Apologies if this was already answered, but I wasn't able to find
it.]

Take this example where I'm looking for the mean across a data set:

> ddply(baseball[,1:5], .(lg), mean)
id year stint team lg
1 NA 1873.338 1.061538 NA NA
2 NA 1887.029 1.093567 NA NA
3 NA 1965.773 1.095733 NA NA
4 NA 1914.568 1.108108 NA NA
5 NA 1958.956 1.090350 NA NA
6 NA 1890.000 1.000000 NA NA
7 NA 1884.000 1.222222 NA NA

It would seem appropriate that the variable "lg" would have been
excluded from the mean() function by default. But in order to run
this properly, this needs to be stated explicitly:

> ddply(baseball[,1:5], .(lg), function(x) mean(x[, !colnames(x) %in% "lg"]))
lg id year stint team
1 NA 1873.338 1.061538 NA
2 AA NA 1887.029 1.093567 NA
3 AL NA 1965.773 1.095733 NA
4 FL NA 1914.568 1.108108 NA
5 NL NA 1958.956 1.090350 NA
6 PL NA 1890.000 1.000000 NA
7 UA NA 1884.000 1.222222 NA

messages.author: dc06d729e023580a
messages.subject: Re: Exclude the grouping variables in ddply?
parts:
Hi Shane,

I've thought about this too, but I don't see any way to implement it
that doesn't end up reducing the generality of the ddply function.
Instead, I recommend explicitly stating you only want to calculate the
mean on numeric columns:

> ddply(baseball[,1:5], .(lg), numcolwise(mean))
lg year stint
1 1873.338 1.061538
2 AA 1887.029 1.093567
3 AL 1965.773 1.095733
4 FL 1914.568 1.108108
5 NL 1958.956 1.090350
6 PL 1890.000 1.000000
7 UA 1884.000 1.222222

Hadley
